abstract: We propose a novel integrated dual-polarization Kramers-Kronig (DP-KK) receiver architecture using a photonic-integrated circuit (PIC) comprising two serially cascaded polarization-selective photodiodes. We validate the concept by experimental demonstration of a 224 Gb/s data signal reception (28-GBd PDM-16QAM) after transmission over 120-km SSMF.

articleTitle: 8007 km C + L band transmission over MCF with 19-core cladding-pumped EDFA
abstract: We investigate an MCF link using a C+L-band, 19-core, cladding-pumped EDFA over trans-oceanic distances measuring a fully decoded throughput of 18.6 Tb/s and 14.5 Tb/s at a distance of 8007 km for an inner and outer-ring cores respectively.

articleTitle: Demonstration of improved performance provided by FOPA for extended PON in burst-mode operation
abstract: We demonstrate amplification of burst mode optical packets under different traffic density by a fibre optic parametric amplifier (FOPA) and compare with EDFA as in-line amplifier after 50 km SMF transmission. These experiments showed a minimum of a 2dB performance improvement of FOPA compared with the EDFA.

articleTitle: Machine learning for performance improvement of periodic NFT-based communication system
abstract: We compare performance of several machine learning methods, including support vector machine, k-nearest neighbours, k-means clustering, and Gaussian mixture model, used for increasing transmission reach in the optical communication system based on the periodic nonlinear Fourier transform signal processing.

Author Keywords: Machine Learning based DSP for optical transmission
Schemes for impairment mitigation increasing data throughout and/or mutual information

articleTitle: Performance-complexity tradeoffs of concatenated FEC for 64-QAM MLC and BICM
abstract: Multilevel coding (MLC) is compared with bit-interleaved coded modulation (BICM) from a performance-versus-complexity standpoint. In both approaches, complexity-optimized error-reducing inner codes are designed for concatenation with an outer staircase code, assuming signaling with 64-point quadrature amplitude modulation. The codes are designed to achieve various points on the Pareto frontier characterizing the performance-complexity tradeoff. Computer simulations of the resulting codes reveal that the MLC approach (a) provides significant advantages compared to BICM and (b) has a clear edge over an existing MLC proposal, providing a net coding gain of up to 13.6 dB at 28% overall overhead, yet with reasonable decoding complexity.

articleTitle: High spectral efficiency superchannel transmission using a soliton microcomb
abstract: We demonstrate transmission of a 52 channel superchannel using an optimized 22.1 GHz-spaced soliton microcomb. Enabling a record spectral efficiency of >10 bits/s/Hz after 80 km and 6.1 bits/s/Hz after 3000 km using a microcomb. Our results demonstrate that chip-scale combs can achieve performance directly comparable to bulk-optic frequency combs.

articleTitle: High density few-mode multicore fibre amplifier for energy efficient SDM transmission
abstract: We present an L-band 6-mode 7-core amplifier supporting 42-spatial channels with a new record low power consumption factor of 0.36 and demonstrate simultaneous amplified SDM transmission with the highest reported spatial density and energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of eight-dimensional modulation formats for long-haul optical transmission
abstract: Two novel 5.5 bit/4D modulation formats are experimentally demonstrated to transmit over 9680 km of SSMF. A reach increase of 29.4% over the 6 bit/4D PM-8QAM is shown. Furthermore, increased nonlinear tolerance with respect to PM-8QAM is shown.

articleTitle: Field trial of real time 200G and 400G flex-rate transmission using 69 GBaud signal
abstract: We report a successful field trial using a flex-rate 16nm CMOS oDSP transceiver over a deployed ROADM network with 200G PDM-QPSK over a 2174 km link and 400G PDM-16QAM with highest reported real-time transmission rate of 69 Gbaud in a 75 GHz grid.

articleTitle: Real-time demonstration of C-band 19.2 Tb/s field trial by constellation shaping 16QAM in 2000-km G. 654.E terrestrial link
abstract: In this paper, we make real-time demonstration of constellation shaping (CS) 16QAM in 2000-km terrestrial field trial. The system has C-band 96 channels with 19.2 Tb/s with 7.2-dB system margin, which is a new record of terrestrial fiber transmission system.

articleTitle: Flexible metro network architecture based on wavelength blockers and coherent transmission
abstract: A flexible semi-filterless architecture for metro DWDM networks with ring- or horseshoe topologies is presented. ROADM nodes are based on wavelength blockers. Coherent transmission enables filterless channel selection. Critical parameters are determined and a 4-span, 160-km horseshoe with 100Gbit/s DP-QPSK and 200Gbit/s DP-16QAM is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Joint optimization of DAC and ADC based on frequency dependent ENoB analysis for high speed optical systems
abstract: We present a novel model that accurately simulates frequency dependent ENoB in ADCs. The model is validated through simulations and experiments. Along with a similar DAC model, we identify electronic converter specifications required for <1 dB OSNR penalties in links employing 64QAM and 256QAM.

articleTitle: Gb/s visible light communication with analogue single-colour LED receiver
abstract: Visible light communication bears the potential to deliver high data rates in the Gb/s range while being robust to electromagnetic interference. To do so, optical wireless systems exploit sophisticated transmitter and receiver sub-systems that appear as too custom for a practical inclusion in most consumer electronics. Instead, we propose the re-use of widely adopted lighting equipment: the light emitting diode. We experimentally demonstrate a conceptually simple laser-sourced 1 Gb/s VLC downlink with a receiver based on a commercial single-colour LED. While adaptive bit-loading is applied for multi-carrier transmission to best exploit the available bandwidth, the penalty due to broadband modulation at 1 Gb/s is minimized through analogue frequency response equalization. By accommodating for duobinary transmission, cost-effectiveness is ultimately provided through the dismissal of broadband analogue-to-digital conversion and digital signal processing.

articleTitle: Radio-over-air with a face-to-face EML transceiver pair
abstract: A coherent-optical free-space link for local cloud radio access networks is proposed and experimentally evaluated. Conceptual simplicity is obtained by reducing opto-electronic sub-system complexity at both link ends to a single externally modulated laser. Full-duplex 64-QAM OFDM transmission over a transparent coherent optical pipe is shown over an optical budget of 21.3 dB, or an estimated reach of ∼100 m in case of bad atmospheric conditions. The penalty in error vector magnitude is less than 1% when compared to a PIN/TIA-based receiver. Cost-effectiveness is achieved by off-loading the directional split in the signal chain to the RF domain and the dismissal of digital signal recovery functions typically associated to coherent reception.

articleTitle: Back-Side-On-BOX heterogeneous laser integration for fully integrated photonic circuits on silicon
abstract: We present a fabrication flow integrating lasers at the backside of silicon-on-insulator wafers. It is expected to be compatible with integration of other material-layers and reduce the variance of lasers performance. A DFB laser fabricated accordingly exhibits a total waveguide-coupled power of 60mW at 160mA/20°C.

articleTitle: Does ageing of margins become more attractive in WDM networks with 64 GBaud transponders and regenerators?
abstract: We analyse on two WDM core networks the benefit achievable by network planning with ageing of margins when considering up-to-date elastic transponders and accounting for both actual routing of channels and intermediate regeneration.

articleTitle: Experimental validation of clipping combined with digital resolution enhancer for high speed optical transmission
abstract: A digital resolution enhancer combined with clipping is experimentally validated by transmitting single channel 600 Gb/s 64-QAM and WDM 460 Gb/s 128-QAM over 75 km, allowing to reduce the DAC's physical number of bits to 3. Low resolution DACs will play an important role in low-power transmitters.

articleTitle: Full-duplex, polarisation-independent coherent homodyne EML transceiver
abstract: A conceptually simple coherent transceiver based on an externally modulated laser is proposed for virtual point-to-point transmission and experimentally evaluated for low-cost access applications. The analogue EML transceiver pair is shown to allow for full-duplex transmission and polarization-independent coherent reception with highly reduced optical layer complexity. The locking stability of the homodyne receiver is confirmed for the injection of 14 data channels and in presence of Rayleigh backscattering at 1 km of drop fibre. An unshared per-user data rate of 2.5 Gb/s is achieved for an optical loss budget of 36.3 dB, without the need for digital signal recovery.

articleTitle: Mode-conversion-based silicon photonic modulator using asymmetric Bragg grating and Y-branch
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a Bragg-grating-based modulator operating in reflection with low loss and without a circulator by using mode conversion and an asymmetric Y-branch. With a compact footprint of 240μm, we demonstrate OOK up to 30 Gbit/s with an estimated switching energy of 150 fJ/bit.

articleTitle: Actively aligned flip-chip integration of InP to SiN utilizing optical backscatter reflectometry
abstract: We present our hybrid III-V/SiN integration interface with a novel active alignment technique overcoming contacting limitations in flip-chip assembly. The interface allows for integration of single chips and full arrays. An average coupling loss of −2.1dB and a record coupled power exceeding 60mW is achieved.

articleTitle: On parameter optimization of product codes for iterative bounded distance decoding with scaled reliability
abstract: We use density evolution to optimize the parameters of binary product codes (PCs) decoded based on the recently introduced iterative bounded distance decoding with scaled reliability. We show that binary PCs with component codes of 3-bit error correcting capability provide the best performance-complexity trade-off.

articleTitle: High-rate continuous variable QKD with optically carrier-suppressed pilot
abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) is considered as a promising solution for the seamless integration of quantum communication technology in optical telecommunication networks due to its overlap with coherent optics. Yet, it has to satisfy the demanding performance requirements such as a low excess noise for its coherent detection process. We will experimentally demonstrate a coherent intradyne CV-QKD system that utilizes an optically phase-locked and polarization-multiplexed pilot tone to enable frequency-offset and carrier-phase estimation of a free-running local oscillator at the receiver. A low excess noise of 0.022 shot-noise units is yielded through optical carrier suppression for the training signal, which enables high secure-key rates of 89 Mb/s in a 4.2 km short-reach scenarios or 4.3 Mb/s over a 40-km field-deployed fibre link.

Author Keywords: Demonstration of point-to-point quantum communication systems

articleTitle: Experimental characterization of Perturbation-induced modal birefringence in few-mode fibers
abstract: A technique to distributedly evaluate the perturbation-induced effective refractive index variation on the higher order modes of a few-mode fiber is presented. The technique is based on spectral correlation analysis and has been experimentally validated for the LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> and LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> modes of a 6-modes few-mode fiber.

articleTitle: Multi-vendor sliceable transceivers in partial disaggregated metro networks
abstract: We experimentally assess the concept of multi-vendor programmable sliceable transceivers based on multicarrier modulation, tailored for partially disaggregated optical metro networks. The OpenConfig vendor-neutral data model is envisioned for the implementation of the SDN agents. Transceiver advanced capabilities are enabled further exploiting network flexibility.

Author Keywords: Integration of optical transmission and networks with higher layer network services

articleTitle: First field-trial of a high capacity micro-comb based optical communications system
abstract: We present the first demonstration of micro-comb based communications system in installed optical fibre. Robust soliton-crystal states enable open-loop control, and achieve 32.5 Tb/s (8.2 b/s/Hz spectral efficiency) over 72.8 km, providing a path to compact, high capacity transceivers for legacy fibre, metro-area systems.

articleTitle: Mirror-based silicon-photonics vertical I/O with coupling efficiency enhancement for standard single-mode fiber
abstract: A broadband, low polarization-dependent silicon-photonics vertical coupling was demonstrated based on an integrated curved mirror. Owing to its lens function, coupling efficiency between a silicon inverse taper waveguide and a standard single-mode fiber was enhanced by 1.4 and 3.4 dB for TE and TM polarization.

articleTitle: 100 Gbps simplified coherent PON using carrier-suppressed PDM-PAM-4 and phsae-recovery-free KK detection
abstract: We propose and demonstrate, for the first time, a simplified coherent TDM-PON based on low-cost DFB lasers, MZM modulated with carrier-suppressed PDM-PAM-4 signal and Kramers-Kronig receiver without frequency offset estimation and phase recovery. 29dB/27dB power budgets are achieved for 100Gbps signal after 25km/40km downstream transmissions.

articleTitle: Estimating transmission capacity with probabilistically shaped 64-QAM
abstract: We discuss three different capacity estimation methods for transmission using probabilistically shaped modulation formats. We experimentally demonstrate ∼70 Tb/s transmission over 6,970 km using probabilistically shaped 64QAM with multi-stage nonlinear compensation and compare this result to capacity measurements using multi-dimensional coded modulation.

articleTitle: 7-Core × 6-mode photonic lantern mode multiplexer
abstract: We present a high spatial density few-mode multicore photonic lantern mode multiplexer, able to selectively excite LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf>, LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11a,b</inf>, LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21a,b</inf> and LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> modes in an hexagonal array of 7 cores with low insertion loss, using a fluorine-doped microstructured glass template.

articleTitle: Strategies for organic VLC: Effects of clipping on the performance of multi-band CAP modulation with polymer-based light-emitting diodes
abstract: We investigate, for the first time, the effect of signal clipping on multi-band carrier-less amplitude and phase (m-CAP) modulation in visible light communications based on PLEDs. We experimentally demonstrate a Q-factor improvement up to ∼2.25 dB can be obtained with a clipping level of 50%.

articleTitle: Enhancing the security of OFDM-PONs with machine learning based device fingerprint identification
abstract: We propose and demonstrate an identity authentication method in OFDM-PON by recognizing device fingerprints of ONUs. Experimental results show that rogue ONU can be detected and 92.43% identification accuracy is achieved. The proposed method can effectively improve the ability of PONs to resist identity spoofing attack.

articleTitle: 450-GHz-wave beam-steering with 1 kHz repetition by optical phase control
abstract: Beam-steering is an effective method for future terahertz-wave wireless communications because the power is concentrated to a certain direction. A 2×8 optical phased array was designed and fabricated using a silica-based lightwave circuit for THz phase control, and 450-GHz-wave beam-steering with 1 kHz repetition was demonstrated.

articleTitle: Silicon photonic components for 400 Gb/s transceivers
abstract: Growing demand for data transmission capacity is driving a rapid evolution of optical component architectures and requires photonic technology that combines high levels of photonic integration and functionality with low cost and rapid product ramp capabilities. In this talk, we will present an overview of Intel Silicon Photonics technologies and components developed to address 400 Gb/s pluggable transceiver applications and to scale to the next generation Tb/s optics and integrated optical IOs.

articleTitle: Digital 4K video transmission over realtime water-air OWC-OFDM system with low-complexity transmitter-side DSP
abstract: A real-time 2.2-Gb/s water-air OWC system is successfully demonstrated with low-complexity transmitter-side DSPs, namely, geometric shaping and a joint PAPR reduction. With the DSPs, the system achieves a significant 8-dB ROP improvement at a BER of 3.8×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>, and it enables four 4K-video transmissions.

articleTitle: Silicon photonics based 16λ-WDM demultiplexers for operating in C-band and O-band spectral regimes
abstract: We proposed novel 16λ demultiplexer and experimentally demonstrated polarization diversified operation with 32 Gbps NRZ signal transmissions in C-band range. We also verified the operation of proposed scheme in O-band range.

articleTitle: Low thermal sensitivity hollow core fibre for optically-switched data centre applications
abstract: We demonstrate 20-times greater tolerance to temperature variation using hollow core fibres compared to SMF-28 in a fast optical switching system. With frequency and once-only phase synchronisation, we obtained error-free transmission of short packets with <625ps clock recovery time in 25.6 Gb/s real-time systems.

articleTitle: Kernel affine projection for compensating nonlinear impairments in optical direct detection systems
abstract: We propose a novel kernel affine projection (KAP) algorithm, which combines kernel mapping and affine projection for channel equalization in optical direct detection systems. Experimental results show that the KAP algorithm can mitigate nonlinear impairments in short-reach communications while maintaining low computational complexity.

articleTitle: Characterization of crosstalk-impaired OOK signals in WC-MCF systems with high and low skew×bit rate
abstract: The received amplitudes of crosstalk-impaired on-off keying signals in weakly-coupled multicore fibre (WC-MCF) systems are experimentally assessed for high and low skew×bit-rate. Gaussian-distributed crosstalk-induced amplitudes are shown for high skew×bit-rate. The mean of these amplitudes can also be modelled by Gaussian distributions.

articleTitle: 16×200 GBPS virtual carrier assisted DD transmission over 80 km with only 14 GHz of digitizer bandwidth
abstract: By employing a 112 GSa/s SiGe BiCMOS 1-to-4 ADC front-end, we demonstrate a WDM direct detection transmission with a net data rate per channel of 200 Gb/s over 80 km using only 14 GHz of receiver's digitizer bandwidth

articleTitle: Single-stage scheduler for accurate QoS delivery in virtualised multi-tenant Passive Optical Networks
abstract: We propose a single-stage downstream scheduler assuring accurate Quality of Service delivery across Virtual Network Operators in a multi-tenant PON. We show performance close to an ideal scheduler in the ability to control QoS and compare performance to that of standard schedulers.

articleTitle: Statistical characterization of intermodal crosstalk in direct detection schemes: M-PAM versus DMT
abstract: Transmissions over multimode fibers can be done using different techniques, nevertheless, inter-model crosstalk is a main limiting factor for high data rate transmissions. We characterize the statistics of the inter-modal crosstalk in direct detection M-PAM and DMT systems and assess their relative advantages and disadvantages

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of SiPh Flex-LIONS for bandwidth-reconfigurable optical interconnects
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate the first 8-port SiPh Flex-LIONS, a bandwidth-reconfigurable switching fabric based on wavelength routing and space switching. Experimental results show error-free one-to-eight multicast interconnection at 25 Gb/s and bandwidth reconfiguration from 25 Gb/s to 100 Gb/s between selected input and output ports.

articleTitle: Highly spectral efficient transmission of 183 + 24.5 GBaud 256-QAM spatial super channels over 55 km three-mode fiber
abstract: We investigate the data-rate increase of 256-QAM over 64-QAM signals in few-mode fiber transmission. Simulations and experimental validation indicate an increased total data throughput by applying 256-QAM, achieving 146 Tbit/s total data-rate at an average spectral efficiency of 10.67 bit/s/Hz/mode over the entire C-band.

Author Keywords: Demonstrations of transmission benefit from combined novel fibres
Lab and field implementation of optical fibre transmission links

articleTitle: Non-hermetic and compact 4-wavelength integrated ROSA for 400 Gbps (4 × 100 Gbps)
abstract: We developed the smallest 4-wavelength integrated receiver optical sub-assembly (ROSA) to our knowledge. Our ROSA is comprised of an LC receptacle, a flexible printed circuit (FPC) and a plastic frame without using hermetic sealing. Four photodiodes (PDs) and one 4-ch transimpedance amplifier (TIA) are mounted on the FPC and the plastic frame including an optical de-multiplexer (ODEMUX) is adjusted to obtain appropriate PD responses. We achieved the receiving performance required for 400 Gbps 2 km application over an operating temperature range of −10 °C to 90 °C. The minimum receiver sensitivity was −8.3 dBm at 90 °C and a lane-to-lane crosstalk penalty was less than 0.1 dB.

articleTitle: 200km Repeater length transmission of real-time processed 21.2Tb/s (106×200Gb/s) over 1200km fibre
abstract: We demonstrate real-time transmissions of 21.2Tb/s (106×200Gb/s PM-16QAM) and 15.9Tb/s (106×150 Gb/s PM-8QAM) over 1206 km TeraWave<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">¯</sup> SCUBA-125 fibre at 201 km amplifier-span length with 1.5dB and 3.9dB Q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-factor margin, respectively.

articleTitle: 8 × 8 Silicon photonics multicast switch with on-chip integrated 2 × 4-ch SOAs
abstract: We demonstrate an 8×8 silicon photonics multicast switch with on-chip SOAs. The number of SOA channels was extended by flip-chip bonding of two 4-ch SOAs. The on-chip SOAs exhibited a net gain of ∼9 dB. With careful design and fabrication, lossless transmission will be feasible.

articleTitle: Integrated 5-bit microwave photonic beamformer for broadband phased array antenna applications
abstract: We report a microwave photonic beamformer on the silicon photonics platform. It contains a modulator, 8 switchable 5-bit true-time delay lines, and 8 photodiodes. The beam angle can be steered from −63.16° to 58.12° with a step of 4° for X and Ku bands.

articleTitle: Wafer-scale folded micro-optical interconnects
abstract: An innovative wafer-scale micro-optical solution for compact 90° optical interconnects is presented. In particular, micro-optical structures were designed and fabricated, which redirect the light using total internal reflection (TIR). The micro-optical interconnects consist of either a quarter ball lens (Q-lens) or a 45° micro-prism, both fabricated using wafer-scale UV imprint. Finally, the folded micro-optical elements are combined with integrated self-alignment structures, which easily enable passive fiber self-alignment and packaging.

articleTitle: A novel programmable disaggregated edge node supporting heterogeneous 5G access technologies
abstract: We demonstrate a programmable disaggregated edge node in support of both metro and long-haul networks. This solution is successfully evaluated through Bristol's City Metro Network, over 100km and 200km optical fibre with a low power penalty.

articleTitle: 100GBaud QAM signaling with silicon photonic electro-absorption modulators
abstract: We demonstrate up to 100 GBaud QAM signal generation with silicon EAM based I/Q-modulator. Single-polarization QPSK signaling at symbol rates of 50 GBaud and 100 GBaud with BERs below the soft-decision FEC limit is shown. 16QAM signals at symbol rates of 50 GBaud are generated in a differentially driven configuration.

articleTitle: 53 GBd PAM-4 DAC-less low-power (1.5 pJ/b) silicon integrated transmitter
abstract: We present an integrated PAM-4 transmitter consisting of two parallel GeSi electro-absorption modulators wirebonded to a SiGe BiCMOS driver, consuming 160mW excluding laser. 53GBd PAM-4 transmission is demonstrated over more than 1km fiber and 2km non-zero dispersion-shifted fiber, without using equalization or digital signal processing.

articleTitle: Joint detection equalization on Nonlinear Fourier Transform based optical communication
abstract: We propose a joint detection based equalization of noise caused by the Nonlinear Fourier Transform itself. In experiments we achieve a gain of 4.4 dB at a bit error rate of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup> and a slight range increase for long-haul transmissions.

articleTitle: Vector mode inter-modal wavelength conversion in a dispersion tailored highly nonlinear few-mode fibre
abstract: We present the design and fabrication of a dispersion tailored highly nonlinear few-mode fibre with an inter-modal nonlinear coefficient of 2.81 (W · km)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, the highest reported to date. Inter-modal wavelength conversion between the HE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> and TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> vector modes is demonstrated in the fibre.

articleTitle: Demonstration of on-line bi-directional 10-RRHS with an 80 Gbit/s/RRH capacity using 256 QAM WDM coherent transmission for next generation mobile fronthaul
abstract: We demonstrate the construction of 10 RRHs with 10 ch-WDM, 80 Gbit/s-256 QAM bi-directional real-time coherent transmission for high-capacity next generation mobile fronthaul.

articleTitle: Probabilistic shaping-assisted bit-energy efficient THz photonic wireless transmission
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a transmission of beyond 60 Gbit/s probabilistically shaped 16-QAM signals over a 4.5 m 350 GHz photonic wireless link, achieving a reduced energy consumption per bit of 1.38e-17 J/bit/m compared to the uniform format.

articleTitle: Mapping strategies for short-length probabilistic shaping
abstract: Mapping techniques for probabilistic amplitude shaping are reviewed. We focus on energy considerations, classification of methods and systems, and implementation aspects. A numerical study of required block lengths is carried out for two short-blocklength applications, namely achieving half of the maximum shaping gains and enabling rate adaptivity.

articleTitle: On the performance of scalable fast optical switch based recursive network architecture for HPC applications
abstract: We investigate a novel scalable low-latency HPC network for blade-to-blade interconnection exploiting multiple-parallel recursive architecture with fast optical switches under realistic HPC application traffics. Compared with Leaf-Spine HPC interconnecting 4096-blade, results show that HFOS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> reduces up to 75.9% latency, 64.2% cost and 30.9% power consumption.

articleTitle: Wavelength-tunable in-series DFB laser array in good single-longitudinal-mode operation
abstract: We proposed a 4-channel 100-GHz-spacmg in-series DFB laser array m good single-longitudinal-mode operation. Based on the reconstruction-eqmvalent-chrrp technique, a long linear-chirped Bragg grating with multiple λ/4 phaseshifts are implemented in the laser cavity. The proposed structure paves a way for the wavelength-tunable in-series DFB laser array.

articleTitle: On the impact of intercore skew on joint-core carrier-phase estimation
abstract: The impact of intercore skew on joint-core carrier-phase estimation in multicore-fiber transmission is studied. It is shown that the performance degradation is not dependent on the combined linewidth of the light-source laser and the local oscillator, but rather the ratio between the two linewidths.

articleTitle: Demonstration of a novel framework for proactive maintenance using failure prediction and bit lossless protection
abstract: We propose a novel framework for proactive maintenance that realizes disruption-free networks with low latency. The proactive replacement of failure predicted parts is demonstrated based on diagnoses of optical fiber bend estimates and bit lossless protection in optical transport networks.

articleTitle: Wide-wavelength range membrane laser array using selectively grown InGaAlAs MQWs on InP-on-insulator
abstract: We have successfully demonstrated selective-area epitaxial growth of InGaAlAs MQWs on thin InP layer on SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si substrate for developing an eight-channel membrane laser array with a lasing wavelength of 1272.3–1310.5 nm. By optimizing the photoluminescence peak for each laser, 25.8-Gbit/s direct modulations are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Ultra-low power 32-channel × 50-Ghz grid tunable wavelength (de)multiplexer in SOI
abstract: We demonstrate a thermally tunable 32-channel silicon cascaded Mach-Zehnder (de)multiplexer with 50 GHz spacing. An ultra-low tuning power of 2.98 mW per channel per free spectral range (mW/channel/FSR) was achieved with suspended phase shifters. The effectiveness of the (de)multiplexer was confirmed by high-speed transmission experiments.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of scalable and reconfigurable optical generation of a 240-Gbit/s super-channel using a single stage of multi-subchannel nonlinear wave-mixing and optical frequency comb
abstract: We experimentally demonstrated a scalable and reconfigurable optical generation of a 240-Gbit/s super-channel using a single nonlinear wave-mixing stage and an optical frequency comb. Three 20-Gbaud 16QAM sub-channels are demonstrated with 0.7 dB OSNR penalty. The reconfigurability is investigated with different baud rates and modulation formats.

articleTitle: Experimentation based development of a simulation platform of a microwave photonics MIMO imaging system
abstract: We present the conception, a system simulation and an experimental validation of an innovative high-speed, high-resolution microwave photonics imaging system for security applications, working at microwave or millimetre frequencies and introducing single-shot and single-channel acquisition photonics technologies for real-time target detection.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of a PON technology-based optical transport solution over field installed DSF
abstract: This paper reports the first field trial of an optical transport solution that exploits NG-PON2 technology while using standard EDFAs. Error-free Ethernet transmission over a 10-Gbps/λ optical sub-lambda path through 252 km of field-installed DSF with deterministic frame latency is successfully demonstrated.

articleTitle: On-chip multi-channel reconfigurable optical delay line array with dynamic power equalization
abstract: We design and fabricate a multi-channel reconfigurable optical delay line array by means of switching the optical paths, based on silicon-on-insulator platform. The device provides 6-bit by 8-channel delay with dynamitic power equalization. High delay resolution and low power difference between different channels are achieved.

articleTitle: Phase-sensitive OTDR strain measurement using single mode operation in multimode OM4 fiber
abstract: We present the first realization of strain sensing in a multimode OM4 optical fiber using phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry. We demonstrate that single mode operation in an OM4 fiber is achievable and allows the fiber strain to be measured in a distributed manner. The 4 km of OM4 fiber is effectively measured with 20 cm spatial resolution which proves that coherent Rayleigh scattering based techniques can be used to interrogate multimode optical fibers.

articleTitle: A novel CAP equalizer for 112 Gb/s data transmission over 150 m MMF links
abstract: 112 Gb/s data transmission over 150 m MMF with a BER within the HD-FEC threshold is experimentally demonstrated using a novel equalizer type and CAP modulation. A ∼2 dB receiver sensitivity improvement over an adaptive DMT scheme is achieved for a 100 m MMF link.

articleTitle: 106 Gbit/s PAM4 60-km fibre-amplifierless transmission using SOA assisted extended reach EML (AXEL) with average output power of over 9 dBm
abstract: We fabricated an electroabsorptive modulated laser with an integrated semiconductor optical amplifier (AXEL) with high modulated output and superior extinction characteristics. A record 60-km 106 Gbit/s PAM4 modulation transmission was successfully demonstrated by using the AXEL transmitter with high average output of 9.1 dBm

articleTitle: Coding for optical communications — Can we approach the Shannon limit with low complexity?
abstract: Approaching capacity with low complexity is a very challenging task. In this paper, we review and compare three promising coding solutions to achieve that, which are suitable for future very high-throughput, low-complexity optical communications.

articleTitle: ANN-based multi-channel QOT-prediction over a 563.4-km field-trail testbed
abstract: We demonstrated an ANN-based multiple-channel QoT predictor over a 563.4-km field-trial testbed. The proposed ANN-based approach predicted Q-factors of the planning unestablished channels and the existed channels with maximum error of 0.06dB. The predictions provide important prior-information for dynamic reconfigurations of low-margin optical networks.

articleTitle: Quantum limited optical receivers in the presence of intersymbol interference
abstract: The ISI effect due to the dead time of practical photon counting receivers is studied. Using both the counts and arrival times of photons, a novel demodulation technique is proposed showing sensitivity levels around 7 dB beyond traditional photon counting schemes.

articleTitle: Comparison of entropy loading and bit loading in short-reach optical links
abstract: We show the system performance comparison between the entropy-loading (EL) and bit-loading in multicarrier short-reach optical links where the responses of the low-cost optoelectronic components are less than ideal. We show that EL could be critical for short-reach interconnects to squeeze out the last few bits from the bandwidth-constrained systems.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of tunable and reconfigurable spectrum sharing of two asynchronous QPSK data channels using power division multiplexing
abstract: We have experimentally demonstrated tunable and reconfigurable spectrum sharing of two asynchronous QPSK data channels using power division multiplexing. Both 20 Gbaud strong and 9 Gbaud weak signals are demodulated with BER below FEC using successive interference cancellation, and they can have different baudrates and modulation formats.

articleTitle: Efficient 110 Gbit/s OOK transmitter using silicon hybrid popymer modulator
abstract: We demonstrated a low voltage driving 110 Gbit/s OOK transmitter using hybrid silicon modulator with efficient EO polymer. It reaches BER below HD-FEC threshold just with a drive voltage of 1.4 Vpp. It has also shown a good thermal operation at temperature up to 100°C.

articleTitle: Broadband cognitive radio enabled by photonics
abstract: Concept of photonics-based cognitive radio is proposed, benefiting from broadband spectrum sensing, ultrafast signal processing, and high-efficient spectral resource allocation enabled by photonics. A demonstration of the photonics-based cognitive radar is performed.

articleTitle: Finding transport network configurations using supervised machine learning
abstract: We propose a machine learning-based approach using a random forest for the fast computation of optimized transport network routing configurations. An evaluation in a 7-node network shows that our approach achieves competitive results in terms of solution quality and computation time compared to an exact ILP solution.

articleTitle: Split-enabled 490 Gb/s optical interconnect with direct detection NOMA-CAP and 7-core multi-core fibre
abstract: NOMA-CAP modulation format has been experimentally demonstrated using a 2 km MCF with 7 spatial channels and a PIN-based direct-detection receiver, resulting in a maximum aggregated traffic of 490 Gb/s with negligible transmission penalty.

Author Keywords: Novel digital signal processing algorithms for optical transmitters & receivers
High capacity optical transmission for data centre intra-connections

articleTitle: Reduced footprint multiplane light propagation mode multiplexers
abstract: We design, assemble and characterize three different multiplane light propagation (MPLC)-based mode multiplexers, including a device with reduced size, supporting 45, 45 and 36 spatial modes, respectively. Ranging from 2700mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> to 146mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, all devices achieve <−12 dB cross talk, showing that MPLC can enable compact multiplexers.

articleTitle: Silicon-photonics based remote-radio-head using mode and wavelength division multiplexing with capacity of 4.781 Tbit/s for radio-over-fiber massive MIMO
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a silicon-photonics (SiPh) remote-radio-head (RRH) supporting 96 channels for radio-over-fiber (ROF) massive multiple-input-and-multiple-output (MIMO) application. 4×4 Mode-division-multiplexing (MDM) and 24 wavelength-division-multiplexing (WDM) ROF channels are combined to achieve a total capacity of 4.781-Tbit/s.

articleTitle: Optical networking for 5G Xhaul and service convergence: Transmission, switching and control enabling technologies
abstract: The paper provides an overview of the 5G Xhaul network in terms of architecture, transmission, switching and control to provide a convergent infrastructure for supporting all service including IoT. Challenges and relevant aspects are described, providing concrete examples of solutions and related open issues.

articleTitle: Narrow-linewidth thermally tuned multi-channel interference widely tunable semiconductor laser
abstract: Narrow-linewidth thermally tuned multi-channel interference (MCI) widely tunable semiconductor laser is demonstrated, which realizes a tuning range of more than 45 nm (covering the whole C-band), side mode suppression ratios up to 56 dB, Lorentzian linewidth around 200 kHz and total micro-heater tuning power below 50 mW.

articleTitle: Intra- and inter-datacentre converged networks utilising Kramers-Kronig receivers
abstract: Intra- and inter-datacentre traffic is now exploding. To process both kinds of traffic cost-effectively, intra- and inter-datacentre converged network architectures that use cost-effective transponders are needed. In this paper, we propose a novel network architecture based on Kramers-Kronig (KK) receivers. KK-receiver-based systems can handle both intra- and inter-datacentre traffic more cost-effectively than coherent systems and attain higher transmission quality than legacy non-coherent systems. To confirm the feasibility of our proposed network architecture, we construct part of a 640×640 optical circuit switch and evaluate its performance when handling intra-datacentre traffic and inter-datacentre traffic; chromatic dispersion is managed in the receiver-side digital signal processing. 80 wavelengths in the C-band are fully evaluated through bit-error-ratio measurements.

Author Keywords: Intra and inter data centre networks

articleTitle: Demonstration of using multiple orthogonal spatial modes for channel header information and channel encoding
abstract: We demonstrate using OAM modes to carry header information of a signal for routing. We show encoding the header on a single OAM mode or a codeword of multiple OAM modes. We observe 0.4–0.8 dB penalty for 10 Gb/s OOK signal switched at 10Mb/s rate.

articleTitle: Four-channel interference tunable semiconductor laser
abstract: We demonstrate a low-cost tunable laser by utilizing the constructive interference of four channels. A tuning range of 32nm with SMSRs above 40dB across the whole tuning range is achieved. The device is promising for use in WDM-PON.

articleTitle: Multisymbol periodic nonlinear Fourier transform communication
abstract: In this work, for the first time, a full-spectrum periodic nonlinear Fourier-based optical communication system with exact inverse transform is introduced and its performance in a fibre link with ASE noise is evaluated in terms of Q-factor and BER through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Si racetrack modulator with III-V/Si hybrid MOS optical phase shifter
abstract: We successfully demonstrated a Si racetrack modulator with III-V/Si hybrid MOS optical phase shifter exhibiting V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">π</inf>L of 0.064 Vcm. Compared with a MZI modulator with the same phase shifter, the racetrack modulator reduced the energy consumption by three quarters without expense of the modulation bandwidth.

articleTitle: Membrane III-V/Si DFB laser with width modulated silicon waveguide for narrowing linewdth
abstract: We demonstrate a membrane laser using an InP-based active region combined with a 220-nm-thick Si waveguide, where the Si waveguide width at the middle of the cavity is wider. The laser with a 500-μm long cavity exhibits a 3.3-mA threshold current and ∼300-kHz Lorentzian linewidth.

articleTitle: Transmitter I/Q cross-talk post-compensation using receiver DSP
abstract: Performance degradation of high-order modulation and high baud-rate systems due to transmitter electrical I/Q cross-talk inherent in photonic integrated circuits is characterized. A post-compensation technique based on receiver-side DSP is proposed. The cross-talk level requirement for 64QAM 64GBaud is reduced from −30dB to −24dB.

articleTitle: Integrated electrically-pumped quantum-dot microlasers with tunable single-mode operation
abstract: Electrically-pumped micro-ring lasers with azimuthal gratings were designed and fabricated using InAs/InAlGaAs/InP quantum-dot structures grown by MOCVD. Continuous-wave single-mode lasing covering 1300 nm to 1370 nm with SMSR over 40 dB was achieved. Tunable single-mode operation and on-chip integration with waveguide and SOA/photodetector are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Lattice pilot aided DMT transmission for optical interconnects achieving 5.82-Bits/Hz per lane
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate 276-Gbps net rate 128QAM-DMT transmission at soft-FEC limit in an IM/DD system with a single C-band packaged EML, a DAC and a photo-detector, proposing a lattice pilot algorithm for channel equalization with only 1% overhead reaching spectral efficiency of 5.82-bits/Hz per lane.

articleTitle: To C- or not to C-, that is the question
abstract: Equal capacity C- and L-band unrepeatered links with high-order Raman co- and counter distributed amplification were compared. Experiments using 40 channels with 100 GHz subcarrier-based frequency-domain 8-dimension advanced modulation format have shown that the budget of the L-band link was ∼ 2 dB higher.

articleTitle: Theoretical analysis of maximum transmit power in a b-modulator
abstract: The optimal transmit power in various nonlinear Fourier transform-based transmission systems has been observed to decrease with the signal duration when bandwidth is fixed. A new theoretical explanation for this behavior is provided for a specific b-modulator and validated in simulations.

articleTitle: Full frequency domain model for strong nonlinear third order parametric processes
abstract: In this paper we report a novel full frequency domain model for modeling strong third order nonlinear parametric processes. As an example we use fibre optical parametric amplifiers to assess the validity of the model.

articleTitle: Advanced waveguide bends for photonic integrated circuits
abstract: The reduction of bending loss from 0.06 to 0.01dB/90° by an advanced shape on a silicon nitride waveguide bend of 20μm-radius for 850nm is experimentally demonstrated. Theoretical study also shows losses are decreased from 0.05 to 0.02dB/90° in a silicon waveguide bend of 2μm-radius for 1550nm.

Author Keywords: fabrication and characterisation of novel integrated devices and functionalities

articleTitle: Four-dimensional polarisation-ring-switching for dispersion-managed optical fibre systems
abstract: The recently introduced 4D 64-ary polarisation-ring-switching format is investigated in dispersion-managed systems. Numerical simulations show a reach increase of 25% with respect to PM-8QAM. This gain is achieved from the nonlinear tolerance of the format and a 4D demapper using correlated noise assumptions.

articleTitle: Quantum communication in fiber channels with polarization dependent loss
abstract: We propagate entangled photons through telecom fiber channels. Our experiments demonstrate the resilience of polarization entanglement to the aggregate polarization dependent loss of channels with and without additional polarization mode dispersion. Furthermore, we demonstrate a Procrustean PDL-mitigation scheme and discuss its rate-quality trade-off.

articleTitle: A route-and-select optical switch with flip-chip-bonded LVDS-compatible driver for sub-nanosecond switching
abstract: We present a monolithically integrated route-and-select optical switch comprising Mach-Zehnder interferometers and electro-absorption modulator gate array; realized on SI-InP substrate to isolate the active sections without epitaxial regrowth. Using a flip-chip bonded HEMT driver operated with LVDS input signals, 0.64-ns optical switching is demonstrated.

articleTitle: A 160 Gb/s (4×40) WDM O-band Tx subassembly using a 4-Ch array of silicon rings co-packaged with a SiGe BiCMOS IC driver
abstract: We demonstrate a 4-channel O-band transmitter comprising a Silicon Photonics RM array co-packaged with a SiGe BiCMOS integrated dnver chip. 4×40 Gb/s data modulation with an average ER of 3.39 dB is reported, with the transmitter module exhibiting a high energy efficiency of 2.52 pJ/bit.

articleTitle: Direct amplitude-phase modulated dual-EML 10 Gb/s optical transmitter
abstract: We demonstrate a simple 8-ary coherent transmitter by simultaneous amplitude and phase modulation of an integrated dual-EML. Results at 10 Gb/s indicate enhanced sensitivity and narrower channel spacing compared with conventional PONs, demonstrating its feasibility for next generation access networks with low-complexity coherent transceivers.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of utilizing adaptive optics to mitigate intra-modal-gronp power conpllng of few-mode fiber in a two-channel 20-Gbit/s QPSK mode-division-mnltiplexed system
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate utilizing adaptive optics to mitigate intra-modal-group power coupling in LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode group for two-channel 20-Gbit/s QPSK mode-division-multiplexing transmission. Power penalty of < 2 dB and < 5 dB are achieved for the two channels, respectively.

articleTitle: High bandwidth coupled multicore fibre for data centre applications
abstract: A coupled multicore fibre with 165 cores is designed and fabricated. The fibre has a peak modal bandwidth of 8.4 GHz·km in the 850 nm window. Error free 25 Gb/s transmission over 150 m of the fibre is demonstrated using a VCSEL based transceiver.

articleTitle: First demonstration of a two-layer all-optical neural network by using photonic integrated chips and SOAs
abstract: We demonstrate the first all-optical feed-forward neural networks constituted by two full photonic layers of neurons based on SOAs with Broadcast and Weighting protocol. The impact of optical nonlinear function is studied and signal processing with 10 Gbit/s binary sequences is presented which results in 0.21 error.

articleTitle: V-Groove assisted passive assembly of single-mode fibers to ultra-broadband polarization-insensitive edge couplers for silicon photonics
abstract: We demonstrate SiN-based edge couplers with better than −1.5dB/fiber coupling efficiency to SMF28 fibers for both TE and TM polarization in O- and C-band. V-Groove assisted passive assembly of 80 μm reduced-cladding fibers to these edge couplers is also demonstrated with −2dB/fiber coupling efficiencies.

articleTitle: Coexistence of 11.2 Tb/s carrier-grade classical channels and a DV-QKD channel over a 7-core multicore fibre
abstract: We successfully demonstrate coexistence of record-high 11.2 Tb/s (56×200Gb/s) classical channels with a discrete-variable-QKD channel over a multicore fibre. Continuous secret key generation is confirmed together with classical channel performance below the SDFEC limit and a minimum quantum channel spacing of 17nm in the C-band.

articleTitle: Tunable dual-wavelength coupled-cavity semiconductor lasers
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate twin-microsquare and microsquare-Fabry-Pérot (FP) coupled-cavity semiconductor lasers. By adjusting the injection currents, dual-wavelength lasing with tunable frequency differences ranging from ∼12 to ∼235 GHz and a wavelength tuning range of ∼10 nm is respectively achieved for the twin-microsquare and microsquare-FP lasers.

articleTitle: Ultra-compact silicon-graphene waveguide device for high-speed wavelength conversion
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate an ultra-compact silicon-graphene wavelength converter at a 28-Gb/s data rate. A four-wave mixing conversion efficiency of −28 dB is achieved in the silicon-graphene strip waveguide with a 60-μm-long light-graphene interaction length using a moderate pump power.

articleTitle: Application-based dynamically reconfigurable optical network on chip architecture
abstract: We propose an application based dynamically reconfigurable optical network on chip architecture and a power efficient reconfigurable optical router structure. The simulation results show the reconfigurable architecture can reduce path-setup delay by 70% compared with Torus and 43% compared with Firefly under a dynamic traffic.

articleTitle: Practical innovations enabling scalable optical transmission networks
abstract: We review and expand on key optical innovations that enable scalable and efficient optical fibre transmission to meet continuing bandwidth growth. We will present recent industry-leading technology trials giving real-world experience of ground-breaking technologies in field deployed optical networks.

articleTitle: Addressing practical challenges in quantum cryptography
abstract: We discuss the current landscape in quantum cryptography in the context of future quantum-safe communications and describe the state-of-the-art and practical challenges in this field, focusing in particular on continuous-variable quantum key distribution systems and on efforts towards their miniaturization and their integration into standard telecommunication networks.

articleTitle: Reflow-solderable bridging fibres for efficient coupling with silicon photonic devices
abstract: Bridging fibres for efficient coupling with silicon photonic devices are developed. Thermally expanded core technique is applied to single-mode and polarization-maintaining fibres. Splice losses of 0.1 dB with standard fibres are achieved by optimizing internal glass structure. High-temperature resistant coating enables reflow soldering compatibility.

articleTitle: The EML as frequency-coded optical neuron
abstract: Neuromorphic photonics is considered as one of the key enables that support the convergence of optics and information technology. In its endeavour to realise neuro-inspired circuitry at high speed, low latency and high interconnect density it unleashes a plurality of novel applications such as analogue optical processing and accelerators or optical neural networks. The basic building blocks do not necessarily have to be complex. A basic opto-electronic device as simple as an externally modulated laser can already mimic the function of an optical neuron in the optical frequency domain. It responds to excitatory and inhibitory inputs, provided that their particular weights exceed the excitation threshold. I will show that these parameters can be mapped in spectrum and power in case of the proposed EML implementation and experimentally validate spiking behaviour under both types of stimuli for 5-GHz pulse characteristics.

articleTitle: High-speed multi-signal power equalisation for flexible optical path operation
abstract: We have developed an acousto-optic-tunable-filter based flexible optical power equalising system that collectively controls multiple-wavelength signals within 3 microseconds for agile optical networks. We have demonstrated that our system can appropriately equalise 4-wavelength signals with dynamically fluctuated power.

articleTitle: Nonlinear optics in multimode fibers
abstract: We overview the emerging field of nonlinear optics in multimode optical fibers, which enable new methods for the ultrafast light-activated control of temporal, spatial and spectral degrees of freedom of intense pulsed light beams.

articleTitle: Multimode-waveguide based temperature-insensitive silicon Mach-Zehnder interferometer and cascaded filter
abstract: A temperature-insensitive Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) based on one single multi-mode silicon waveguide is demonstrated on SOI platform. The device shows a thermal dependence around 13pm/°C in a wavelength range of 40nm. A cascaded filter is further built based on the proposed MZI.

articleTitle: Loss reduction in hollow-core conjoined-tube negative-curvature fibre
abstract: We review recent progress on hollow-core conjoined-tube negative-curvature fibres. One fibre with loss of 2 dB/km at 1512 nm and one with 3.8 dB/km loss at 680 nm is presented. The latter approaches the Rayleigh scattering loss limit of silica fibre at that wavelength.

Author Keywords: Specialty optical fibres for improved transmission performance
Low-latency fibres and fibres for new wavelength ranges

articleTitle: Wide field-of-view 1-to-4 optical multicasting for bi-directional indoor optical wireless communications using CAP modulation
abstract: We demonstrate point-to-multipoint bidirectional indoor optical wireless communications (OWC) over 4 meters using fibre-based transceivers. It is between a spatial light modulator (SLM) based beam steering base station with ±30° field-of-view (FOV) and four nomadic user terminals that use mirror-based beam steering with ±50° FOV. We design our indoor OWC system to integrate with fibre-to-the-home/building (FTTH/B) networks enabled by the second next-generation passive optical network (NG-PON2) technologies. At the SLM based beam steering base station, a composite phase mark is constructed based on the locations of the four user terminals and all-optically multicasts an infrared narrow beam at a NG-PON2 designated wavelength to the user terminals. From the mirror-based nomadic terminal to the base station (the upstream direction), light at a different designated wavelength is transmitted along the same optical path as the downstream and steered back to the fibre network by the constructed phase mask. Bandwidth efficient carrierless amplitude and phase modulation-16 (CAP-16) scheme is employed to transmit 24 Gbit/s in both upstream and downstream. We achieve bit error rate (BER) well below the hard decision forward error correction (FEC) threshold for both the downstream and upstream transmissions.

articleTitle: FPGA demonstration of adaptive spacetime compression towards high-fidelity, low-latency 5G fronthaul
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate 8-antenna MIMO fronthaul uplink enabled by the first FPGA-based adaptive space-time compressor. 48Gb/s CPRI-equivalent rate encapsulating 1024QAM 5G NR-grade signals is transported using as low as 2.5GBd optical PAM4, achieving <1.25% EVM and 50ns latency for compression.

articleTitle: Multiport micro-optic devices for hollow core fibre applications
abstract: Using micro-optic collimator technology, we present fully integrated 3-port hollow-core-fibre (HCF) components (e.g. 1×2 beam-splitter and WDM coupler), thereby increasing the diversity of inline HCF components and facilitating the use of HCF in a broader range of fibre optic applications.

articleTitle: Graphene modulators in silicon photonics platforms
abstract: We review the state of the art of graphene modulators in silicon photonics platforms. Results obtained in the fabrication of single and double layer capacitive modulators are reported showing intensity and phase modulation, operation up to 50 Gb/s and chromatic dispersion resilience.

articleTitle: 72 GBd graphene-on-plasmonic slot waveguide photodetector
abstract: We present an ultra-compact graphene-on-plasmonic slot waveguide photodetector with active size of 90 nm × 100 nm × 6 μm, which shows a responsivity of 300 mA/W, a 1.5-dB bandwidth exceeding 70 GHz and 72 GBd high-data rate reception for communication band of 1550 nm.

articleTitle: TDD-based rerouting in layer-2 network with time aware shaper technique for accommodating mobile front-haul and IOT
abstract: Time division duplex-based rerouting is proposed for Internet of Things traffic in Layer-2 network accommodating mobile front-haul by time aware shaper technique. A performance evaluation showed that the bandwidth efficiency was improved by 1.8 times on average while maintaining the low mobile front-haul latency.

articleTitle: Quasi-single-mode transmission with reduced multipath interference by distributed Raman amplification
abstract: For the first time, we show numerically and experimentally that multipath interference can be reduced significantly by distributed Raman amplification (DRA) in quasi-single-mode transmission. By optimizing the intensity overlap between LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> & LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> modes, the required number of equalization taps can be reduced by 3.5 times.

Author Keywords: Fibre and Free Space Devices and Fibre Amplifiers

articleTitle: Simultaneous RF signal self-interference cancellation, optoelectronic oscillator and frequency down-conversion for co-frequency co-time full duplex 5G communication
abstract: We propose a novel method to simultaneously realize wideband RF signal self-interference cancellation, optoelectronic oscillator, and frequency down-conversion using only one single-polarization optical IQ modulator. 5×20MHz LTE-A signal with central-frequency of 12.6GHz is down-converted to 2.6GHz and about 28dB cancellation ratio is achieved experimentally.

articleTitle: Telemetry-driven validation of operational modes in openconfig disaggregated networks
abstract: A novel provisioning workflow to validate vendor-proprietary transmission solutions in disaggregated, multi-vendor networks is proposed and implemented. The workflow exploits an OpenConfig NETCONF Agent implementation enhanced with gRPC telemetry to assess and retrieve transmission performance and rapidly determine the most suitable operational mode.

articleTitle: 103-GBd PDM-16QAM coherent detection highly tolerant to transmitter IQ impairments enabled by real-valued 4 × 4 MIMO equalizer
abstract: We propose a novel receiver side DSP based real-valued 4 × 4 MIMO equalizer for transmitter IQ impairment mitigation in coherent systems. Experiment on 103-GBd PDM-16QAM signal shows our proposed algorithm can tolerate 3.8-dB IQ imbalance or more than 2-ps skew at 1-dB OSNR penalty.

articleTitle: A GN/EGN-model real-time closed-form formula tested over 7,000 virtual links
abstract: We derived a fully-closed-form GN-model formula and tested its accuracy of over 7,000 highly randomized C-band system scenarios. By further applying a correction that leverages the large system test-set, we were able to substantially improve it and obtain EGN-model accuracy with real-time-compatible computation effort.

articleTitle: High bandwidth all-optical fiber-based neuromorphic signal processing
abstract: We introduce the first all-optical concept based on optical fiber, which enables dual-quadrature signal processing with high bandwidth. We demonstrate the gain over 2 dB for 64-QAM and over 3 dB for 256-QAM of the proposed technology over linear equalisation for standard fiber-optic communication links.

articleTitle: Reduced-complexity chromatic dispersion compensation method
abstract: A novel algorithm to compensate CD using only one FFT operation is presented. Experimental results indicate that the proposed formulation achieves equivalent performance as the FDE technique with overlap-save reconstruction for transmission distances from 1,000 km to 10,000 km at potentially half the complexity.

articleTitle: Joint optimization of probabilistic shaping and forward error correction
abstract: We investigate the joint performance of PS and FEC, reviewing optimization techniques for designing spatially coupled codes and distribution matching. We exemplify that room for further performance improvement by PS is relatively small compared to FEC by estimating the gap to the Shannon limit.

articleTitle: Performance model and design rules for optical systems employing low-resolution DAC/ADC
abstract: We establish resolution requirements for digital/analog interfaces supporting 600 Gb/s and beyond by proposing a performance model accounting for quantization and clipping noises isolated from the ENoB. We experimentally show a good model accuracy, prediction error being less than 0.5dB in the regime of interest.

articleTitle: Mitigation of inter-subcarrier linear crosstalk with fixed frequency-domain equalizer assisted MIMO for high-order modulation
abstract: We experimentally demonstrated inter-subcarrier linear crosstalk mitigation of 25-GBaud RRC-PM-16/32/64QAM dualsubcarrier, using the fixed frequency-domain equalizer assisted MIMO. The proposed method showed the robustness for modulation formats, and enabled 15.8 % tighter subcarrier spacing over 80 km SSMF, compared to the conventional 2×2 MIMO.

articleTitle: Method for a comprehensive evaluation of margins in optical networks
abstract: We propose a unified approach to assess the combined impacts of guard bands, performance margins and optical protection on spare network resources, mainly to quantify how much capacity can be yielded through margin reduction schemes.

articleTitle: How to slice and dice your switch capacity
abstract: Datacenter network cost can be reduced by exploiting the trade-off between port speed and switch radix in favor of more, but slower ports. To enable this architectural change, the cost ratios between optics and switches and between narrow and wide optical link types must shrink.

articleTitle: A novel hybrid polling algorithm for packets contention resolution in optical switching based data center network
abstract: We demonstrate a novel hybrid polling algorithm for optical packets contentions resolution (HPACS) for OPSquare data-centre network based on fast optical switches. Results show that the HPACS reduces 46.47% latency, and 18.73% packet-loss at traffic load >0.5 compared with traditional packet retransmission contention resolution.

articleTitle: Observing the generalized SNR statistics induced by gain/loss uncertainties
abstract: We performed a Monte-Carlo analysis to observe how the linear and nonlinear contributions to the generalized SNR vary with the uncertainties of gains and losses in line systems. We show variations up to 2.5 dB with spectrally dependent uncertainties of the two components.

articleTitle: Physical-layer aware routing, modulation level and resource allocation of SDM networks over FM-MCFs
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel physical-layer aware routing, modulation, spatial and spectral resource allocation scheme for few-mode multi-core fibres (FM-MCFs) relying on an analytical formula for calculating OSNR. Additionally, we compare different flavours of the proposed algorithm in terms of their network-wide performance.

articleTitle: Piecewise linear equalizer for 56 Gbit/s PAM-4 signal transmission using DML with large adiabatic chirp
abstract: Computationally efficient piecewise linear (PWL) equalizer is, for the first time, proposed to compensate amplitude-dependent skews caused by DML chirp and chromatic dispersion. 56 Gbit/s PAM-4 signals in C-band are respectively enabled for 40 km and 60 km transmission below the HD-FEC and SD-FEC.

articleTitle: Suppressing waveform distortion in phase-OTDR vibration sensing for visualising optical fibre cable state
abstract: For risk assessment of communication failure, Φ-OTDR vibration measurements are used to visualise optical fibre cable states. We reveal that conventional high-sensitive Φ-OTDR distort large vibration waveforms. The double-averaging method combined with frequency-division-multiplexing proposed herein is shown to well suppress the distortion.

articleTitle: Network coding enabling resilient 5G networks
abstract: A resilient 5G Network solution adopting Network Coding in the optical transport with minimum buffering requirements is proposed. Network level modelling results demonstrate a 33% reduction in the overall optical network capacity required and 50% reduction of edge node buffer size.

articleTitle: Extension of the ONF transport API to enable quantum encryption in end-to-end services
abstract: The ONF Transport API enables to support transport services like topology or connectivity setup for optical networks. We propose, implement and demonstrate extensions to enable Quantum Encryption in optical end-to-end services.

articleTitle: How to integrate machine-learning probabilistic output in integer linear programming: A case for RSA
abstract: We integrate machine-learning-based QoT estimation in reach constraints of an integer linear program (ILP) for routing and spectrum assignment (RSA), and develop an iterative solution for QoT-aware RSA. Results show above 30% spectrum savings compared to solving RSA with ILP using traditional margined reach computation.

articleTitle: Autonomic SDN control of multi-adaptive OFDM-based BVTs in fully-disaggregated SDM/WDM fronthaul networks
abstract: We present a multi-adaptive OFDM-based BVT controlled with YANG/NETCONF by an autonomic SDN controller for fully disaggregated SDM/WDM fronthaul networks. The autonomic SDN controller deploys a control loop that monitors the per-subcarrier SNR and computes the optimal constellation based on the actual signal degradation.

Author Keywords: Integration of optical transmission and networks with higher layer network services

articleTitle: The training based feed-forward 2×2 MIMO algorithm and its real time implementation
abstract: We propose a training based MIMO algorithm to achieve ultrafast polarization tracking, which directly estimates the Jones matrix of the fibre channel without the adaptive tap updating process, also free of the frequency/phase offset effects. Its implementation in FPGA can track 17Mrad/s polarization scrambling.

articleTitle: Configurations of pump injection and reinjection for improved amplification efficiency of turbo cladding pumped MC-EDFA
abstract: We investigated configurations of cladding pumped MC-EDFA with pump recycling to improve optical amplification efficiency. Spatial injection fibre reinjection with spatial splitting configuration offers additional 3.5 dB of optical gain and 3.5 dB of output power, compared to standard cladding pumping without pump recycling.

Author Keywords: Multimode & multicore fibre and fibre amplifiers for spatial division multiplexing

articleTitle: Probabilistic spectrum Gaussian noise estimate for random bandwidth traffic
abstract: A probabilistic spectrum Gaussian noise (PSGN) model is proposed to predict the nonlinear noise for random bandwidth traffic in long-haul elastic optical networks. The model reduces the noise estimate 9.1% on average compared to the standard Gaussian noise model applied to the maximum bandwidth.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable mode OADM demonstration in weakly-coupled 10-mode-division multiplexed network
abstract: Reconfigurable mode optical add/drop multiplexer (M-OADM) demonstration in weakly-coupled 10-mode-division multiplexed (MDM) network testbed was conducted using 32-Gbaud DP-QPSK signals. Optical add/drop multiplexing of 10 spatial modes and mode switched paths over 96 km have been successfully demonstrated.

Author Keywords: Highly parallel network and interconnect demonstrations
Design of high connectivity node architectures including protection and failure recovery

articleTitle: Calibration of polarization skews in optical coherent transceiver based on digitial signal processing
abstract: An accurate and wide range calibration scheme that simultaneously measures the transmitter and receiver polarization skews only by receiver side DSP is proposed. Experiment shows the calibration error is less than ±0.3ps over 30ps range.

Author Keywords: Novel digital signal processing algorithms for optical transmitters & receivers

articleTitle: Low-complexity dual-stage soft failure detection by exploiting digital spectrum information
abstract: We propose a novel digital spectrum feature extraction method and demonstrate its effectiveness. Dual-stage soft failure detection structure is employed to reduce the overheads for monitoring and detection. False positive rate of 0.14% and false negative rate of 1.41% are realized.

articleTitle: Enabling simultaneously optimum performance and minimum cost of frequency offset estimation with sparse-FFT-assisted monitoring scheme
abstract: We propose a blind and robust monitoring scheme of frequency offset drift based on sparse fast Fourier transform, by which optimum performance and minimum hardware-cost of frequency offset estimation are achieved simultaneously. The performance is experimentally verified with 28 Gbaud QPSK, 16- and 64-QAM signals.

articleTitle: Performance characterisation of ultra-wideband Raman amplifiers
abstract: We experimentally characterise the performance of two different 150nm (1470–1620nm), ∼14dB gain Raman amplifiers consisting of hybrid distributed-discrete and discrete-discrete configurations. The hybrid scheme improves S-band OSNR and Q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-factor of 120Gb/s PM-QPSK signals after 63km transmission by <4dB and 1dB respectively compared to discrete-only design.

articleTitle: A self-adaptive microwave photonic bandpass filter
abstract: We present a microwave photonic self-adaptive bandpass filter that performs filtering on the instantaneous frequency of an unknown microwave signal. The filter maintains a bandpass characteristic around the carrier frequency of the incoming signal making it applicable to frequency hopping communications and electronic warfare systems.

articleTitle: Transmission of probabilistically shaped 100 GBd DP-16QAM over 5,200 km in a 100 Ghz spacing WDM system
abstract: We investigate the transmission performance of the PS signals in a bandwidth-limited WDM system. With 100-GHz channel spacing, 100-GBd 16QAM, 100G-Bd PS 16QAM (3.775bit/symbol/pol.), and 106-GBd PS 16QAM (3.775bit/symbol/pol.) can be transmitted over 4000, 5200, and 2000km, respectively.

articleTitle: Analysis of intra-mode coupling length in few-mode fibers
abstract: This work proposes a semi-analytical method to compute the coupling length within groups of degenerate modes in few-mode fibers. The method is then applied to assess coupling for LP modes, in fibers affected by stress birefringence and core ellipticity.

articleTitle: Dynamic reconfiguration in field-programmable photonic arrays
abstract: We demonstrate a dynamic (re)-configuration and parallel multi-tasking in a field-programmable photonic array chip. Its multipurpose functionality is exploited to realise a total of four different circuits, across three optical port combinations, based on recorded presets.

articleTitle: Polarization control in multimode fibers
abstract: By shaping the incident wavefront of a laser beam into a multrmode fiber with strong polarization mixing and random mode coupling, we can either eliminate depolarization and restore the input polarization state, or convert the output fields into any arbitrary polarization states.

articleTitle: Spatial mode overhead transmission using a coupled multi-core fibre
abstract: Novel coupled multi-core fibre (MCF) based spatial mode overhead transmission is proposed. We reveal that mode dependent loss or total transmission capacity can be controlled in terms of the number of overhead modes by utilizing a coupled-MCF with a sufficient number of cores.

articleTitle: Electro-optically tunable laser with < 10-mW tuning power dissipation and high-speeed λ-switching for coherent network
abstract: We developed a novel tunable laser based on the electro-optic effect. The laser exhibited an extremely low tuning-power dissipation of <10 mW for the full C-band and very high-speed tuning of ∼500 ps with a laser linewidth available for conventional coherent systems of <350 kHz.

articleTitle: Fast blind chromatic-dispersion esitimation for small-rolloff Nyquist pulse-shaped signal using spectral cyclostationarity
abstract: A fast blind chromatic-dispersion estimation technique for small roll-off Nyquist pulse-shaped signal is proposed. Our method employs frequency-shift, low-pass-filter and down-sampling procedure added to cyclostationaly-based estimator. Estimation accuracy is experimentally investigated using 96-Gbaud QPSK signal with 0.01 roll-off factor, and compared to conventional methods.

articleTitle: Cross-talk aware channel allocation for all-to-all optical interconnects in sub-optimal AWGR devices
abstract: We propose a crosstalk-aware wavelength-detuning scheme exploiting wavelength reusability to overcome the non-optimal inband crosstalk that limits all-to-all AWGR-based optical interconnections. Experimental validation is demonstrated employing an 8×8 O-band Si-AWGR where simultaneous error-free transmission of 4 pairs of identical signals at 25 Gb/s is achieved.

articleTitle: Demonstration of on-chip 1×4 selective switch with simultaneous mode- and wavelength-division multiplexing
abstract: We demonstrate a silicon photonic 1×4 mode- and wavelength-selective switch that can route six data channels on three modes and two wavelengths simultaneously. The measured inter-modal and intra-modal crosstalk values are below −15 and −20 dB for all the channels, respectively.

articleTitle: Demonstration of proactive bandwidth allocation using LSTM in 5G optical fronthaul
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a proactive fronthaul bandwidth allocation based on the prediction of remote unit (RU) traffic on the Converged Edge Access Network Platform (CEANP). The demonstration results show that the accuracy of the prediction can reach 96% to achieve the proactive bandwidth allocation.

articleTitle: Simultaneous 256 WDM channel generation using a single AlGaAsOI waveguide based time lens source
abstract: We demonstrate simultaneous WDM signal generation using time lens based optical Fourier transformation. Using a single AlGaAs on-insulator waveguide, 256 1-Gb/s WDM channels with 14-GHz spacing are generated from 1570-nm to 1600-nm, and transmitted over a 100-km unamplified link.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of phase-retrieving coherent detection of higher-order modulation formats
abstract: Carrier-less coherent detection based on phase retrieval (PR) is demonstrated for optical higher-order modulation formats. The PR receiver based on a two-dimensional photodetector array and a discreteness-aware PR algorithm successfully demodulated 10-Gbaud optical 16QAM and OFDM signals without using any local lights or optical hybrids.

articleTitle: Performance monitoring for live systems with soft FEC
abstract: A technique to estimate the quality of live traffic transmission, without knowledge of the transmitted bits, is proposed. The technique, which is applicable to systems employing soft forward error correction coding, estimates the so-called asymmetric information from a histogram of L-values.

articleTitle: Routing and spectrum allocation with amplifier placement in elastic metro-aggregation networks
abstract: We propose a quality-of-transmission (QoT) aware heuristic algorithm for the placement of amplifiers in elastic metroaggregation networks with the objective of minimizing their number while guaranteeing lightpaths' QoT. Results show that optimized amplifier placement can lead to significant reduction of amplifiers with respect to baseline approaches.

articleTitle: Picojoule-per-bit coherent links through co-design of photonic and electronic ICs
abstract: The scaling of CMOS and BiCMOS processes with silicon photonic devices will realize energy-efficient coherent transmitters and receivers for short reach (< 2km) applications. We review the principles of coherent links and discuss co-design of electronic and photonic circuitry to optimize QPSK modulation and demodulation.

articleTitle: Measurement of modal attenuation and crosstalk in spliced few-mode fibres based on mode-resolved BOTDA
abstract: We propose and experimentally demonstrate a novel technique based on mode-resolved BOTDA with two optical frequencies. The proposed technique obtains all possible loss and crosstalk values of LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode at splice points in FMFs, and is valid for splice point characterisation.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of a WDM-compatible polarization-diverse OAM generator and multiplexer in silicon photonics
