abstract: We design and demonstrate a WDM-compatible polarization-diverse OAM generator and multiplexer. OAM modes with orders from −3 to +3 are generated directly in circular polarization (left or right) within the wavelength range of 1540 nm to 1557 nm.

articleTitle: Impact of a mixed SMF/MMF-fibre optical distribution network on the performance of 10 Gbit/s TDM-PON trnsmission
abstract: We investigate experimentally the merger of legacy multi-mode fibre campus or in-house infrastructures with single-mode fibre based TDM-PON systems. Impulse response, static and dynamic loss analysis and BER evaluations of different MMF/SMF combinations reveals that 10 Gbit/s systems require 5-10 dB of power margin to function stable.

articleTitle: An uncooled EML packaged in novel TO-CAN for beyond 53 Gbaud PAM4
abstract: An uncooled EML packaged in novel TO-CAN demonstrated f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3dB</inf> of 50.1 GHz. For 53 Gbaud PAM4, TDECQ of 1.4dB was obtained in laser temperature of 20 °C to 80 °C at 0.7 Vpp. A 64 Gbaud PAM4 operation with TDECQ of 2.3dB was also demonstrated.

articleTitle: Quick OPM recreation and robust telemetry in emergency optical networks for early disaster recovery
abstract: We propose an approach for quick-recreation of OPM in disaster recovery and for achieving robust-telemetry, to flexibly adapt the emergency C/M-plane network to post-disaster bandwidth changes. We implement a testbed and demonstrate for the first time a new best-effort OPM capability for efficient disaster recovery.

articleTitle: Vibration identification over 50km SSMF with Pol-Mux coded phase-OTDR
abstract: We demonstrate multi-detection and recognition of mechanical events over 50km of SSMF with coherent homodyne phase-OTDR using novel Pol-Mux orthogonal interrogation codes. Pattern identification of an engine noise is highlighted, paving the way for numerous smart-city/industrial monitoring applications over already deployed telecom fibers.

articleTitle: Novel fibre termination identification employing local light injection and 1.31/1.55-μm-band coherent OTDR
abstract: We propose a novel fibre identification technology based on local light injection/detection and two-wavelength coherent optical time domain reflectometry. We show that our method can identify whether optical fibres are connected to an optical network unit or terminated with a connector or a disconnected fibre.

articleTitle: Delivery of 1.196-Tb/s signal over 800 M based on RF/FSO convergence
abstract: We demonstrate a hybrid RF/FSO converged system consisting of two FSO links and two RF links. 1.196-Tb/s wireless signals are delivered over 800-m converged RF/FSO links. Kramers-Kronig scheme, probabilistic-shaping algorithm, and simplified wireless architecture at W-band are introduced in the system for the first time.

articleTitle: Multiuser visible light communications using OFDMA
abstract: A multiuser visible light communication system using orthogonal frequency division multiple access (OFDMA) is proposed. Each user is assigned a set of OFDM subcarriers with optimised signal power and modulation. In a multi-cell structure, the subcarrier sets are strategically reused to maximize the total throughput.

articleTitle: Self-suppression of signal-signal beating interference using a split-carrier transmitter
abstract: A transmitter-side carrier tone is applied to suppress SSBI in a 112 Gb/s double sideband IM/DD system using a split-carrier transmitter. This novel, low-complexity approach achieves comparable performance to a computationally-intensive linearised receiver without any additional opto-electronic hardware or linearisation DSP.

articleTitle: Monolithic InP 4 × 4 optical unitary converter for all-optical MIMO demultiplexing
abstract: We fabricate and experimentally demonstrate 4×4 optical unitary mode converter monolithically integrated on InP. Based on the multi-plane light conversion concept, reconfigurable 4-mode sorting and switching are demonstrated. We also observed clear eye opening of 40-Gb/s non-return-to-zero signal.

articleTitle: On the effect of in-band crosstalk margins for optimized format selection in meshed optical networks
abstract: We evaluate a service provisioning mechanism to strike a balance between overly pessimistic/optimistic in-band crosstalk penalty estimation in meshed networks. Simulations show that optimizing in-band crosstalk margins according to the topology and routing pattern can help extend capacity for lower-cost networks with high nodal degrees.

articleTitle: Demonstration of polarization-insensitive coherent 56-Gb/s/λ PAM-4 PON using real-valued Alamouti coding combined with digital pilot
abstract: A simplified and polarization-insensitive coherent intradyne detection for 56-Gb/s/ λ PAM-4 PON is experimentally demonstrated by using real-valued Alamouti coding combined with digital pilot. Over 42 and 41 dB power budgets are achieved after 20-/50-km SSMF transmission under the 7% FEC threshold, respectively.

articleTitle: Clustering algorithm for detection in the discrete nonlinear fourier spectrum
abstract: Expectation maximization clustering of received nonlinear spectral data from solitonic pulses is used to reduce bit error rates. Simulations over a 1800 km Raman amplified fiber link demonstrate the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Efficient Germanium variable optical attenuator at 1.95μm wavelength using spin-on-glass doping
abstract: We demonstrated efficient carrier-injection Ge variable optical attenuator (VOA) operating at 1.95 μm wavelength. Owing to spin-on-glass doping for PIN junction formation, Ge VOA exhibited modulation efficiency of 320 dB/A despite short carrier lifetime, resulting in better trade-off between efficiency and bandwidth than Si VOA.

articleTitle: High-power 10-channel WDM laser array fabricated with a holographic lithography step
abstract: We present a 10-wavelength distributed Bragg reflector laser array with a channel power of <13 dBm at 200-GHz spacing. The gratings are fabricated with a single holographic exposure. Multiple wavelengths are achieved through both active tuning of gratings and angled waveguides in the grating region.

articleTitle: A broadly tunable noise radar transceiver based on digital feed-forward lasers referencing
abstract: We present an innovative photonics-based, broadly tunable noise radar transceiver that exploits a digital feed-forward lasers noise referencing architecture both for removing the phase noise introduced by the free-running lasers exploited in the receiver stage, as well as for generating the reference signal used for range and velocity detection via cross-correlation with the received microwave radar returns. The transmitted microwave noise waveform is generated by simply heterodyning a broad-linewidth laser with a tunable local oscillator laser, avoiding the use of bulky RF arbitrary waveform generators and synthesizers, instead allowing the use of low cost, commercially available components with a small size, weight, and power footprint. Reconfigurable operation up to 50 GHz and a ranging resolution of 0.8 m is demonstrated, limited by the available laboratory equipment.

articleTitle: Collective self-learning by exchanging ML models
abstract: Collective self-learning based on Machine Learning (ML) model sharing and combination is proposed to accelerate ML-based algorithm deployment. The considered architecture is presented, together with different alternatives for combining ML models. Performance analysis is carried out on an illustrative use case for autonomic optical transmission.

articleTitle: Hybrid E/O switching adaptive traffic scheduling strategy leveraging flow prediction in intra-data centre networks
abstract: This paper first proposes a hybrid switching adaptive traffic scheduling strategy supported by a DB-LSTM based rack-scale traffic prediction approach in hybrid electrical/optical mtra-data centre networks. Results confirm that the proposed strategy enables congestion-free rack-to-rack communication and high network performance under heavy traffic load scenario.

articleTitle: Latency aware task peer offloading in multi-access edge computing with metro optical interconnection network
abstract: We propose a latency aware task peer offloading scheme for overloaded server in MEC system based on EON. The heuristic algorithm is developed to improve the performance of network latency and resource utilization by jointly optimizing routing and computing resources allocation.

articleTitle: A QoS-aware network reconfiguration method in data centers based on deep reinforcement learning
abstract: We demonstrate a dynamic network reconfiguration method (ACRO) based on deep reinforcement learning that can autonomously learn the scheme to reconfigure the application traffic with different QoS requirements. Numerical results based on real application traffics indicate that the ACRO provides up to 24.6% network latency improvement.

articleTitle: Crosstalk-independent loss measurement along two-mode fibres based on OTDR with transfer matrix estimation
abstract: We propose a novel OTDR-based technique that eliminates the influence of modal crosstalk on measured waveforms by estimating transfer matrices at crosstalk-inducing points and reconstructing the waveforms. The losses along two-mode fibres that have crosstalk-inducing splices can be successfully obtained without being affected by crosstalk.

articleTitle: Performance comparison of probabilistically shaped QAM and hybrid shaped coded modulation APSK formats
abstract: We study and compare performance of PS-QAM formats (SE=3.6–8.6b/s/Hz) and CM-APSK formats (SE=4.8–8.8b/s/Hz) with hybrid shaping. We show that CM performs slightly better than PS formats in back-to-back and transmission with our hardware and implemented FEC. Similar NLC benefit is observed for both format.

articleTitle: Robust dithering based stabilization for quantized LMS adaptation
abstract: Analog fractionally-spaced equalizer (FSE) is an efficient equalizer, however, the FSE might become unstable when sign-sign least mean square (SS-LMS) is used. Here, an analytical model of the instability is derived, and an efficient dithering-based stabilization process is proposed.

articleTitle: Hitless wavelength-selective switch based on single microring resonator embedded with an equal armed MZI
abstract: We demonstrate an optical hitless wavelength-selective switch based on single micro-ring resonator embedded with an equal armed Mach-Zehnder interferometer. It can simultaneously operate at multiple different wavelengths at the distance of times of FSR as a comb filter and without wavelength blocking during switching.

articleTitle: Virtual carrier-to-signal power ratio enhancement for Kramers-Kronig receivers
abstract: We propose a novel scheme to increase virtual carrier-to-signal power ratios for Kramers-Kronig receivers at the receiver side. We demonstrate that the optimal carrier-to-signal power ratio can be reduced by up to 3 dB, and obtain the optical signal-to-noise ratio improvement of 2.1 dB.

articleTitle: Symbol-rate digital signal processing for low-complexity polarization diversity intradyne optical PSK receivers
abstract: We implement and evaluate a DSP for short-reach coherent intradyne receivers with simple clock recovery that uses only one sample per symbol for data processing. It enables polarization-diversity with reduced hardware complexity and real-time operation on FPGA with DPSK data at 1.25 Gbps per user.

articleTitle: Magnetless on-chip optical isolators
abstract: Optical isolator waveguide devices were fabricated in bias-magnet-free iron garnet films. Slab waveguide devices exhibited isolation > 30 dB and losses ∼ 0.2 dB. Ridge waveguide devices exhibited > 25 dB isolation and loss < 2 dB. A reflection mode isolator concept was experimentally proven.

Author Keywords: Integrated Optoelectronic Devices and Optical Processors

articleTitle: Optical frequency comb noise characterization using machine learning
abstract: A novel tool, based on Bayesian filtering framework and expectation maximization algorithm, is numerically and experimentally demonstrated for accurate frequency comb noise characterization. The tool is statistically optimum in a mean-square-error-sense, works at wide range of SNRs and offers more accurate noise estimation compared to conventional methods.

articleTitle: Combining phase-sensitive amplifiers with DSP for enhanced nonlinearity mitigation
abstract: We investigate combining phase-sensitive optical amplifiers (PSAs) with a static Volterra nonlinear equalizer (VNLE) to mitigate residual nonlinear distortions. Experiments show that the VNLE reduces penalties from link design and improves Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">BER</inf> by 0.4 dB for a 10-GBaud 16QAM signal in a 10×80-km PSA-amplified link.

articleTitle: Few-mode fibre delay lines with inscribed long period gratings for radiofrequency signal processing
abstract: We propose and experimentally demonstrate distributed radiofrequency signal on a few-mode-fibre device. The inscription of long period gratings at specific locations along the fibre allows the excitation of the higher-order modes while adjusting the modal group delays required for sample true time delay line operation.

articleTitle: 60 GB/S PAM4 low-voltage waveguide Si-Ge avalanche photodiode
abstract: We demonstrate a 60 Gb/s PAM4 waveguide Si-Ge avalanche photodiode (APD) with low breakdown voltage of −10 V. The APD receiver has achieved −16 dBm sensitivity at 50 Gb/s PAM4 with a bit error rate of 2.4×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup>.

articleTitle: First experimental demonstration of Core-to-Core Q-difference compensation in SDM transmission systems
abstract: The Core-to-Core Q-difference compensation scheme in the vector domain was demonstrated on a 4-core-path transmission line composed of multicore fibres and cladding-pumped multicore EDFA experimentally. The Q-difference was significantly reduced to within 0.1 dB from 5.6 dB with improvement of the worst quality SDM channel.

Author Keywords: Lab and field implementation of optical fibre transmission links
Algorithms for DSP in optical transmission systems
Multimode & multicore fibres and fibre amplifiers for spatial division multiplexing

articleTitle: On the bandwidth efficiency of analog and digital RoF for mobile fronthaul transmission link
abstract: Digital RoF (D-RoF) is commonly considered as bandwidth inefficient in mobile fronthaul systems. However, under the constraint of optical channel signal to noise ratio (SNR) and analogue signal distortion, D-RoF can be also equivalently bandwidth efficient compared with analog RoF (A-RoF).

articleTitle: Hybrid FSO/MMW system for high-speed and reliable mobile fronthaul system
abstract: This paper proposes and demonstrates a hybrid FSO/MMW system for high-speed and reliable mobile fronthaul transmission. 100-Gb/s and 50-Gb/s Nyqmst-SCM signals are successfully transmitted over the FSO and hybrid systems, respectively.

articleTitle: Static resource allocation for dynamic traffic
abstract: A flexible offline probabilistic (FOP) algorithm is designed to aggressively accommodate random bandwidth traffic demands in long-haul networks. Compared to algorithms that configure demands according to their maximum bandwidth, the FOP algorithm can save 15% of the spectrum used, accommodating over 99% of the throughput demand.

articleTitle: O-band transmission of 92-GBAUD PAM4 with 20-GHz limitation using nonlinear spectral shaping and 2-memory MLSE
abstract: We propose a combination scheme of nonlinear trellis-coded-modulation and 2-memory MLSE to realize spectral shaping for PAM signal. We show that the proposed technique achieves KP4-FEC threshold for 184-Gb/s 10-km O-band transmission with 20-GHz bandwidth limitation, in which the channel-shortening filter has only 5 taps.

articleTitle: End-to-end learning for GMI optimized geometric constellation shape
abstract: Autoencoder-based geometric shaping is proposed that includes optimizing bit mappings. Up to 0.2 bits/QAM symbol gain in GMI is achieved for a variety of data rates and in the presence of transceiver impairments. The gains can be harvested with standard binary FEC at no cost w.r.t. conventional BICM.

articleTitle: 1.3-Tb/s single-channel and 50.8-Tb/s WDM transmission over field-deployed fiber
abstract: We demonstrate the first WDM transmission experiment on a field-deployed fiber network spanning 93 km with a per-carrier net bitrate <1.25 Tb/s on all 40 channels yielding 50.8 Tb/s at 11.29 bits/s/Hz spectral efficiency using only the C-Band, EDFAs, and one DAC per modulated dimension.

articleTitle: 239.3-Gbit/s net rate PAM-4 transmission using directly modulated membrane lasers on high-thermal-conductivity SiC
abstract: We present a directly modulated membrane laser on high-thermal-conductivity SiC exhibiting >100-GHz bandwidth. A ∼40-GHz relaxation oscillation frequency, owing to low thermal resistance and high optical confinement, and a ∼95-GHz photonphoton resonance are achieved. Net 239.3-Gbit/s PAM-4 transmission over 2-km standard single-mode fibre is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Antiresonant hollow core fibre with 0.65 dB/km attenuation across the C and L telecommunication bands
abstract: We report a hollow core Nested Antiresonant Nodeless Fibre (NANF) with a loss of 0.65dB/km across the full C and L telecommunication bands. The fabricated fibre is 1.23km long, it is effectively single moded over sufficiently long lengths, and is able to transmit data.

articleTitle: An accurate model for system performance analysis of optical fibre networks with in-line filtering
abstract: We show that system performance degradation due to in-line optical filtering by wavelength routing nodes in WDM networks can be correctly modelled using digital communications theory of band-limited channels with linear equalization. Experimental validation using a commercial transponder and fibre nonlinear transmission is presented.

articleTitle: 1.3-Tbps/carrier net-rate signal transmission with 168-GBaud PDM PS-64QAM using analogue-multiplexer-integrated optical frontend module
abstract: We demonstrated a 1.3-Tbps/carrier signal transmission over 200 km in 175-GHz-spaced 4.2-THz WDM configuration. A 168-GBaud PDM probabilistically-shaped-64QAM signal with 7.4-bps/Hz spectral efficiency was generated by an 80-GHz optical frontend module integrated with analogue multiplexers and an IQ-modulator based on indium phosphide technologies.

articleTitle: Digital turbulence compensation of free space optical link with multimode optical amplifier
abstract: We demonstrate digital turbulence compensation using a 12-spatial mode digital coherent receiver with a multimode preamplifier that provides a 6-dB sensitivity improvement. This combination acts similarly to ideal lossless adaptive optics. Coherent superposition of 12 spatial-modes reduced median BER from 0.1 to 1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−5</sup> compared to traditional single-mode detection.

articleTitle: Field trial of dynamic DV-QKD networking in the SDN-controlled fully-meshed optical metro network of the Bristol city 5GUK Test Network
abstract: We demonstrate for the first time a field trial of a fully meshed metro network with dynamic QKD networking capabilities across four optical network nodes in the 5GUK Test Network, where the DV-QKD quantum channels co-exist with classical channels and are dynamically switched and rerouted utilising QKD-aware SDN control.

articleTitle: Demonstration of a 1 PB/S spatial channel network node
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a petabit-class hierarchical SDM switching node with granularity from 10 Tb/s to 1 Pb/s. We address spatial bypassing network scenarios, optical channel grooming, spatial multiplex section protection switching, and optical channels using coupled and uncoupled spatial channels.

articleTitle: Modulation format dependent, closed-form formula for estimating nonlinear interference in S+C+L band systems
abstract: A closed-form formula for the nonlinear interference estimation of arbitrary modulation formats in ultra-wideband transmission systems is presented. Enabled by the proposed approach, the formula is applied to the entire S+C+L band (20 THz) and validated by numerical simulations with experimentally measured fibre data.

articleTitle: Net 800 GBIT/S transmission over 605 km using 99.5 GBaud PDM-64QAM with CMOS digital-to-analog converters
abstract: We demonstrate the transmission over 605 km of a spectrally efficient 800 Gb/s 99.5 GBd polarization division multiplexed (PM) 64QAM channel inserted in a wavelength division multiplexed (WDM) full C-band spectrum, using high-speed CMOS digital-to-analog converters (DAC), with digital and optical spectrum optimization.

articleTitle: Huffman coded sphere shaping with short length and reduced complexity
abstract: A novel probabilistic shaping architecture is proposed which approximates the optimal sphere-bound while utilizing a Huffman tree and binary mapping/demapping based on look-up-tables. A 100 symbol long DM sequence achieves within 0.2 dB of the infinite length asymptote, and is implemented with a LUT of 100 kbit.

articleTitle: Equalizing nonlinearities with memory effects: Volterra series vs. deep neural networks
abstract: On coherent DP-16QAM 600Gb/s back-to-back measurements, DNN equalizers outperform Volterra and memory polynomial Volterra equalizers up to 5th orders at a target BER of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup> by 0.5dB and 0.8dB OSNR, respectively. 4 memory taps are applied. DNN equalizers have the potential for competitive implementation complexity.

articleTitle: 16384-QAM transmission at 10 GBd over 25-km SSMF using polarization-multiplexed probabilistic constellation shaping
abstract: We demonstrate the transmission of 10-GBd polarization-multiplexed probabilistically shaped 16384-ary quadrature amplitude modulation (16384-QAM) over 25.5-km standard single mode fiber (SSMF), with a net single-carrier bit rate of 223.8 Gb/s carrying 22.3 information bits/symbol/2-pol.

articleTitle: Record PM-16QAM and PM-QPSK transmission distance (125 and 340 km) over hollow-core-fiber
abstract: We report on the longest hollow-core-fiber transmission experiments to date. The enabling fiber is a low-loss (1.18dB/km @1550nm) and record-length (4.8km) nested-antiresonant nodeless fiber (NANF). We reached 125km and 340km in this NANF with 32GBaud PM-16QAM and PM-QPSK transmission, respectively, with 61 WDM channels loading.

articleTitle: A model for the generalized droop formula
abstract: We provide a new analytical model that fully justifies the recently disclosed Generalized Droop Formula of the nonlinear signal-to-noise (SNR) ratio in very-long submarine links with power-mode amplifiers, and show its relation with the Gaussian-Noise model SNR.

articleTitle: Enumerative sphere shaping for rate adaptation and reach increase in WDM transmission systems
abstract: The performance of enumerative sphere shaping (ESS), constant composition distribution matching (CCDM), and uniform signalling are compared at the same forward error correction rate. ESS is shown to offer a reach increase of approximately 10% and 22% compared to CCDM and uniform signalling, respectively.

articleTitle: Options for time-sensitive networking for 5G fronthaul
abstract: Mobile networks towards 5G impose increasingly stringent requirement on high throughput, low packet jitter and low latency due to emerging time-sensitive applications. Ethernet-based mobile fronthaul is low-cost and flexible, but lacking in determinism. We review and discuss the options for time-sensitive networking based on Ethernet.

articleTitle: 112-Gb/s PAM-4 uncooled (25°C to 85°C) directly modulation of 1.3-μm InGaAlAs-MQW DFB BH lasers with record high bandwidth
abstract: Record high values of bandwidth (39.6 and 27 GHz) and relaxation oscillation frequency (32 and 21 GHz) at 25°C and 85°C of 1.3-μm InGaAlAs-MQW DFB lasers, incorporating newly proposed buried heterostructure, enable 112-Gb/s PAM-4 modulation and 10-km transmission up to 85°C, for the first time.

articleTitle: A novel soft-aided bit-marking decoder for product codes
abstract: We introduce a novel soft-aided hard-decision decoder for product codes adopting bit marking via updated reliabilities at each decoding iteration. Gains up to 0.8 dB vs. standard iterative bounded distance decoding and up to 0.3 dB vs. our previously proposed bit-marking decoder are demonstrated.
